title: Abstract
summary: Frisch et al. (2012) PLoS ONE study of zooplankton colonization in 48 newly built temporary ponds (0.18–2.95 ha) in a restored wetland in Doñana National Park, Spain, sampled over 21 months. New ponds began with about one third the species richness of reference ponds, but detection of new species did not differ, likely due to turnover in reference ponds. Environmental heterogeneity had no detectable effect. Connectivity, spatial position, and surface area drove colonization in copepods and cladocerans, suggesting dispersal limitation absent in rotifers, possibly due to propagule size and abundance.

title: Introduction
summary: Explains that neutral (island biogeography, unified neutral) and niche theories predict diversity drivers of habitat size, isolation, and heterogeneity, and that metacommunity models (species sorting, neutral, mass effects, dispersal limitation) apply. Notes dispersal is hard to measure in freshwater zooplankton, so colonization rates are used as a proxy, with limits from establishment barriers. Reviews conflicting evidence on dispersal limitation. Describes a study of 48 new temporary ponds versus reference ponds, comparing colonization of cladocerans, copepods and rotifers via spatial and environmental factors.

title: Materials and Methods

nodes.title: Experimental Ponds and Reference Ponds
nodes.summary: Describes a restoration study of 96 experimental temporary ponds in Doñana National Park's Caracoles estate, formerly agricultural land, excavated 2004-2005 in three sizes and two depths, filled by rainwater. Eight nearby natural temporary reference ponds and streambed sites are described, with similar hydroperiods and water chemistry. New ponds lack fish, amphibians, and emergent plants, with sparse submerged plants and few zooplankton-feeding birds. Permits are noted.

nodes.title: Sampling and Faunal Analysis
nodes.summary: Describes monthly zooplankton sampling of new experimental ponds (large, medium, small; isolated or clustered) and reference ponds in Donñana, Spain, from 2005 to 2006, including hydroperiods, dry periods, and sample volumes and filtering. It covers in-situ water measurements (temperature, DO, pH, conductivity, depth) and MANOVA results showing DO and size differences. It explains species identification and richness counting, colonization rate estimation via regression of cumulative richness on inundation days, two-way repeated measures ANOVA comparing groups, and variation partitioning with PCA-based environmental heterogeneity and pond morphometry, connectivity, and spatial predictors.

nodes.title: Zooplankton Colonization Rates in Experimental and Reference Ponds
key_items: Comparisons between Taxonomic Groups and Experimental versus Reference Pools
nodes.summary: Describes the sampling of experimental (60, 125, 250 m) and reference ponds across months, with zooplankton collected, filtered, and identified to species; in-situ water variables were compared between pond types. Colonization rates are estimated by regressing cumulative species richness on inundation days, where the intercept gives initial richness and the slope gives colonization rate. Comparisons test interactions between pond type and taxonomic group (rotifers, copepods, cladocerans) using repeated measures ANOVA.

nodes.title: Variation Partitioning
nodes.summary: Describes a variation partitioning analysis of experimental ponds using partial RDA, with four explanatory groups: environmental heterogeneity (PCA of temperature, pH, DO, conductivity; first two axes, 54% variance), pond morphometry (area and volume), connectivity measures (spatial isolation, ditches, pond connectivity, degree of connection, colonization distance), and spatial PCNM axes. Explains the rationale for partial RDA, permutation significance testing, and pure effects estimation on colonization intercepts and slopes.

summary: Restoration study of 96 experimental temporary ponds in Doñana's Caracoles estate (excavated 2004-2005, three sizes, two depths) compared with eight natural reference ponds. Covers monthly zooplankton sampling (2005-2006), in-situ water variables, MANOVA, species richness and colonization rates via regression on inundation days, repeated-measures ANOVA, and variation partitioning (environmental heterogeneity, morphometry, connectivity, spatial PCNM).

title: Results
summary: Study of zooplankton colonization in new versus reference ponds. Initial species richness was about three times higher in reference ponds, varying by taxon (copepods, cladocerans, rotifers), with no relation to tested variables in new ponds. Colonization rates (species per day) did not differ by pond type but did differ by taxon, averaging 0.09 total, 0.05 rotifers, 0.028 cladocerans, 0.015 copepods. Redundancy analysis linked connectivity, area/volume, and colonization distance to copepod and cladoceran rates, with a PCNM spatial axis also significant for each; rotifer rates were unrelated to any variable.

title: Discussion
summary: A discussion of a large Mediterranean wetland restoration experiment on zooplankton colonization. Key findings: environmental heterogeneity did not affect colonization rates, while connectivity, pond area, and spatial position mattered for cladocerans and copepods but not rotifers. Rotifers colonized fastest and copepods slowest. Colonization rates are compared with prior studies, and the study discusses propagule banks, dispersal stages and vectors (wind, birds, hydrology), dispersal limitation, and the Allee effect. It concludes that spatial signals dominate early community assembly, with local biotic and abiotic factors gaining influence as communities mature. Limitations include unmeasured variables and few reference sites. Table 2 reports adjusted R² and p-values per taxon.

title: Supporting Information
summary: Supporting information for a pond zooplankton colonization study: aerial photo of northern pond cluster with overspill-connected ponds marked; categories of pond connection degree; colonization rate plots for combined zooplankton, copepods, cladocerans and rotifers across experimental and reference ponds; spatial potential-connection figure; PCNM spatial eigenvector maps; table of environmental variables (DO differences significant, pond size differs); species occurrence list; acknowledgments, author contributions, and reference list on dispersal and metacommunity ecology.

title: Supplementary figures, PCNM spatial maps, environmental variables, species list, and acknowledgments for pond zooplankton colonization study
summary: Supplementary material for a study of zooplankton colonization in experimental and reference ponds. Includes figures of colonization rates (cumulative richness versus inundation days) for all taxa combined, copepods, cladocerans, and rotifers; a figure of pool spatial relationships; PCNM spatial eigenvector maps; a table of environmental variables with MANOVA and post hoc results (DO and pond size differed); a species frequency table; references; and acknowledgments for funding and fieldwork help.

title: Author Contributions
summary: The text consists of author contributions (experiments designed by DF and AJG, performed by DF and AB, data analyzed by KC and DF, paper written by all four) followed by a long reference list, mostly from PLoS ONE (July 2012). The references cover island biogeography, dispersal and colonization of freshwater invertebrates and zooplankton, metacommunity theory, community assembly, temporary wetlands in Doñana (Spain), dispersal vectors such as wind, waterbirds, footwear, and animals, copepod and cladoceran identification keys, and statistical methods like PCA, variation partitioning, and forward selection.
